threads.body: This state machine cannot distinguish an absent scope after a present scope. Weaver v0.26.1 emits one resource marker, then a scope marker only for OTLP scope groups whose scope exists; for two groups under the same resource (`scope A`, then no scope), the flattened report is effectively `resource, scope A, signal A, signal B`. `current` therefore remains A and a contracted `signal B` incorrectly passes instead of reporting a missing scope. The report representation needs an explicit null/boundary marker (or per-signal scope metadata), which this loop must consume by resetting `current`; please also add a regression for this ordering.

threads.body: This rule only evaluates Weaver's standalone `instrumentation_scope` sample. Weaver v0.26.1 emits that sample only when either the OTLP scope or its schema URL exists, so a signal with no scope produces no finding at all. Consequently an exact `name`/`version`/`schema_url` expectation—or `{present: true}`—incorrectly passes when the entire scope is absent. Please also evaluate top-level signal samples via `input.instrumentation_scope` and treat a missing scope as an empty object (while avoiding duplicate findings for child samples).

threads.body: `Promise.all` rejects as soon as one provider's flush fails, so `flushBeforeShutdown` enters `sdk.shutdown()` while the other trace/log flush may still be running. This violates the required "await both before shutdown" ordering and can lose telemetry from the still-running flush. Wait for both provider promises to settle within the shared deadline, then propagate a rejected result before proceeding to metrics.

This owning-scope test is skipped in CI: the job that installs Weaver and runs `tools/http/runner/tests` does not install `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc`, and `opentelemetry-test-utils` does not provide that dependency. Consequently the new span-specific policy path is never executed. Install the exporter in that job and make this import mandatory so regressions fail instead of silently skipping.

threads.body: The scope policy matches a span using every raw `span.attributes` value, but the runner's `selects()` matches only attributes retained by `carried_attributes()`, which excludes values with Weaver `type_mismatch` advice. If a match attribute is rejected, the runner treats the span as unmatched while this policy can still attach its scope expectations to it. Align these selectors so scope findings apply to the same spans as count and attribute checks.

replies.body: Deferring this. Weaver evaluates span policies before attribute validation, so type-mismatch advice is unavailable here. Aligning selectors requires broader changes for an edge case involving already-invalid telemetry.
